transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-08
Time: 11:00am PT / 18:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Michael Ortiz (CTO, DataWave), Sara Li (ML Eng), Jamal Reed (SRE), Priya Nair (Product)

Summary:
Goal: Sign off on POC success criteria and acceptance tests (go/no-go), finalize workload sizing and benchmarks, agree timelines and reporting format.

Topics:
- Workload profiles and QPS targets
- Latency and cost thresholds (p95 / avg)
- Accuracy / quality gates (eval pass rates)
- Reporting: spreadsheet + Redwood dashboard export + weekly summary
- Infra access, security checklist, timelines

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side - i'm alex, i'll own the engagement, priya is our se, she'll run the benchmarks.
[00:12] Michael Ortiz: hi all, michael here. want to make sure we close the success criteria today so legal can greenlight the pilot.
[00:18] Priya Kapoor: great. i'll go through the proposed acceptance tests and the runbook, then we can iterate.
[00:32] Sara Li: heads up, our main concern is tail latency at the 95th percentile; customer experience drops a lot if that spikes. also cost is huge — we have to stay within budget.
[00:44] Alex Chen: totally. our template breaks this down into performance (latency/throughput), accuracy/relevance (eval pass rate), reliability (error rate), and cost per 1k tokens.
[00:55] Jamal Reed: and security — we need SOC2 evidence, SSO/SAML, audit logs. we'll need network details for the VPC peering.
[01:06] Priya Kapoor: noted. short run-through of the acceptance tests: 1) Latency: p95 < 300ms for the 256-token profile at sustained 50 QPS; 2) Throughput: sustain 100 QPS burst-to-peak for 60s without >1% error rate; 3) Quality: evaluation harness pass rate >= 92% on our labeled prompt set (we can define scoring); 4) Cost: operational cost <= $0.003/token (or alternative cap $X per 1k tokens) during POC; 5) Reliability: system availability >= 99.5% during test windows.
[01:45] Michael Ortiz: couple quick questions — first, is that p95 on dedicated or hosted? our security team prefers private/VPC but budget may push hosted.
[01:56] Alex Chen: these thresholds are written for Redwood Dedicated profiles but we can map them to hosted variants; priya can show expected delta in latency/cost between dedicated vs hosted.
[02:09] Priya Kapoor: right, dedicated gives lower variance and better tail, hosted is fine if you accept slightly higher p95 and different cost. i'll include both mappings in the runbook.
[02:22] Sara Li: on the quality metric — 92% pass rate — can you define 'pass' more concretely? our product team measures hallucination and factuality differently.
[02:34] Priya Kapoor: yes — we'll use a combination: automated metric (rouge/bertscore) + human spot check. pass = automated score above threshold AND no critical hallucination in 90% of sampled outputs. we'll add clear rubric in the sheet.
[02:50] Priya Nair: what about reporting format? we need something our execs can review weekly, and raw data for our engineers.
[02:58] Alex Chen: proposed: 1) shared Google Sheet (benchmarks template) with raw run outputs, aggregated pass rates, and key KPIs; 2) Redwood dashboard export (CSV/JSON) for metrics and token breakdowns; 3) weekly PDF summary with go/no-go recommendation and change log.
[03:15] Jamal Reed: and the acceptance criteria should include an explicit go/no-go rule: if two of the three primary buckets (latency, quality, cost) fail on final benchmark run, it's a no-go. if only one fails, we do a root-cause and re-run after tuning.
[03:29] Alex Chen: that's exactly what we propose. we'll formalize it: final go/no-go is decided on the final 24-hour run window. two or more primary metric misses = no-go.
[03:40] Michael Ortiz: what's the baseline we use? we have an internal model, plus a vendor A proof we ran last quarter. can we compare side-by-side?
[03:50] Priya Kapoor: yes, bring your baseline outputs. our benchmark harness can replay workloads against multiple endpoints. we'll include a comparative sheet column and relative delta to baseline. caveat: tokenization differences can shift cost numbers; we'll normalize on token counts.
[04:07] Sara Li: timeline question: how long is the POC and when do we run acceptance tests?
[04:12] Alex Chen: target POC length is 3 weeks plus a 48-hour acceptance window. proposed schedule: week 0 (this week) - infra onboarding and sample data; week 1 - baseline runs and tuning; week 2 - sustained/soak runs and final benchmark; week 3 - finalize report and acceptance window. start date target week of 2025-05-19.
[04:35] Michael Ortiz: that sounds doable but we need the SOW and statement of work to be signed.
[04:40] Alex Chen: we'll send a draft SOW with the runbook today/tomorrow.
[04:46] Priya Kapoor: technical detail — for the latency test we want two profiles: 1) short chat (average 64 tokens), 2) long form (256-512 tokens). p95 thresholds differ: we'll use p95 < 200ms for short profile on Dedicated, p95 < 300ms for 256 tokens, p95 < 450ms for 512 tokens as stretch.
[05:07] Jamal Reed: are we using KV cache/prefix caching? some of our live traffic has heavy prefix reuse.
[05:13] Priya Kapoor: yes, caching behavior will be enabled by default in the harness and we will report cache hit rate. acceptance test includes cache-on and cache-off runs to show sensitivity.
[05:25] Michael Ortiz: security — we'll need SOC2 docs, encryption details (KMS/HSM), and SAML config. Jamal will share the contact and requirements after this call.
[05:35] Jamal Reed: yep i'll send an inventory of required artifacts. also need to confirm whether Redwood supports our on-prem HSM or if we use cloud KMS.
[05:43] Alex Chen: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM in our on-prem deployments; for Hosted we support cloud KMS and can provide audit logs. we'll include a matrix in the runbook.
[05:55] Sara Li: small note on metrics: please include both mean latency and p95; also include 99th percentile for long-form jobs.
[06:02] Priya Kapoor: will do. reporting will include mean, p95, p99, error rate, tokenized cost, cache hit rate, and eval pass rate.
[06:12] Michael Ortiz: about cost thresholds — $0.003/token seems aggressive; can we instead set a POC cost cap and let you recommend optimizations?
[06:20] Alex Chen: yes we can set a cap for the pilot and Redwood Optimize will provide quantization and batching recommendations to meet it. the acceptance test will check cost <= cap after implementing basic optimizations (standard quantization profile, batching).
[06:35] Priya Nair: do we need to provide labeled eval prompts now or is that later?
[06:40] Sara Li: we'll provide a 1k labeled prompt subset this week; rest can be added during week 1.
[06:47] Priya Kapoor: perfect. for the acceptance report format: final artifact is a single CSV with run rows, plus an aggregated summary tab and a PDF executive summary. we can also push raw metrics to your prometheus if you want.
[07:00] Jamal Reed: prometheus would be ideal for SRE. we'll share scrape endpoints and we can set up grafana dashboards later.
[07:08] Alex Chen: ok last part: sign-off language. we propose the following go/no-go rule in the SOW: final 24-hour acceptance window — if two or more of (latency p95 thresholds, quality pass rate, cost cap) are missed, the POC is considered no-go. If only one is missed, Redwood and DataWave will conduct one tuning cycle (5 business days) and rerun the acceptance window.
[07:34] Michael Ortiz: that is acceptable. can we add a clause for tie-breaker? like if it's borderline (within 5% of threshold) the teams will meet to review telemetry and decide?
[07:44] Alex Chen: yes, add an 'within tolerance' clause and an explicit telemetry review with raw logs as part of decision.
[07:52] Priya Kapoor: i'll include an acceptance decision rubric with exact formulas for pass/fail, and an examples section with fictitious runs so it's clear.
[08:04] Sara Li: any objections to the weekly sync time? Fridays 10am PT works.
[08:08] Michael Ortiz: works for us.
[08:10] Alex Chen: great. recap of immediate deliverables and owners...
[08:16] Alex Chen: (recap) Alex: send SOW + runbook + benchmarks template; Priya: baseline run and mapping for hosted vs dedicated; Michael/Jamal: provide data + infra contacts; all: confirm weekly sync.
[08:30] Priya Nair: ok sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:34] Michael Ortiz: thanks all, appreciate the clarity. we'll review draft SOW and get legal looped in.
[08:40] Alex Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with documents by tomorrow.

End of transcript.

Notes on acceptance tests and reporting (brief):
- Final acceptance run is a 24-hour window with sustained traffic patterns as agreed; raw logs + aggregated CSV + PDF summary to be delivered within 48 hours of window close.
- Go/no-go rule: >=2 primary metric misses = no-go; 1 miss = one tuning cycle and rerun; tolerance band ±5% triggers manual telemetry review.
- Reporting format: shared Google Sheet (benchmarks), CSV export from Redwood console, and weekly PDF executive summary.
- Benchmarks to include: mean/p95/p99 latency, error rate, tokenized cost, cache hit rate, eval pass rate, comparative delta vs customer baseline.

References shared during call:
- Benchmarks template (link) - "link_to_bench_template"
- Redwood POC runbook (link) - "link_to_runbook"
- Sample SOW draft (link) - "link_to_sow_draft"
